concept.title: Secure Red Hat user accounts with two-factor authentication (2FA)
concept.shortdesc: Red Hat allows users to enable two-factor authentication (2FA) as an additional layer of security for logging in to their Red Hat user accounts.

conbody.p: To ensure Red Hat account access is restricted to the intended user, you can add an extra layer of protection beyond just a password. When two-factor authentication is enabled, you use your password plus a one-time code to log in to your account. Utilizing these two authentication factors ensures that even if an unauthorized individual finds your password, they still can not access your account. For daily access, use an authenticator app on your smartphone to instantly generate a one-time code. Alternatively, generate a list of backup recovery codes to use in case you can not access the authenticator app on your smartphone.
Customers have two options for securing Red Hat user accounts with 2FA:

ul.li: Organizational two-factor authentication. Require all users who belong to a specific organization account to use two factors each time they authenticate by enabling two-factor authentication for the organization. Users will be prompted to enable two-factor authentication upon the first log in attempt after the organization account is enrolled. The Organization Administrator for an account can enable organization-wide two-factor authentication. When enabled, all users on that account must use two-factor authentication for authentication when they log in.

Individual opt-in two-factor authentication. Offer individual users the option to enable or disable two-factor authentication for their Red Hat account. When organizational two-factor authentication is turned on, individual users cannot disable it.

conbody.p: Token support for 2FA one-time codes is limited to smartphones or other devices that can install either of the following applications from the Apple App Store or the Google Play Store:
Google Authenticator and FreeOTP Authenticator are the only supported token generators. Hardware tokens, SMS (text-message) tokens, and other apps are not supported.
conbody.note: The current implementation of two-factor authentication only applies to applications using a browser-based authentication flow. It does not apply to command line authentication flows.
